meta_description: Parametric triggers from satellite and field IoT — loss assessment from five weeks to nine days and basis risk complaints down 64%

blocks.x: Parametric triggers from satellite and field IoT — loss assessment from five weeks to nine days and basis risk complaints down 64%
a crop insurer whose loss adjustment meant adjusters driving fields after weather had already finished the damage. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline season measured the drive: five weeks median from loss event to assessment, 31% of claims disputed on index readings the farmer could not see, and adjustment cost eating 19% of premium.
The index used a weather station that could be 40 kilometers from the insured field. Basis risk was not a modeling footnote; it was the complaint log.

We moved assessment to field truth: parcel-level satellite vegetation indices fused with on-farm IoT soil-moisture and weather stations, parametric triggers calculated per parcel with the inputs published to the farmer, and disputes resolved against the same open evidence the trigger used. Adjusters now verify the exceptions, not the portfolio.
